landmarks.name: Olympic Oval
facts: It was North America's first covered speed skating oval.
It was built for the 1988 Winter Olympics and opened on September 27, 1987.

landmarks.name: Rozsa Centre
facts: It is a concert hall with a Bach organ built by Jürgen and Hendrik Ahrend.

landmarks.name: University Theatre
facts: It is designed for drama and dance and seats 505 people, beside the Rozsa Centre.

landmarks.name: MacEwan Student Centre
facts: It is an extension of the students' hall that opened in 1988.

landmarks.name: MacEwan Hall
facts: It is the students' union building and concert venue, known as MacHall.
The first act to perform here was Ian & Sylvia, on October 13, 1967.

landmarks.name: Taylor Family Digital Library
facts: It is the main library and even has a video game collection.
In 2011 it replaced the MacKimmie Library as the university's main library.

landmarks.name: Science A
facts: It opened in October 1960 as the Science and Engineering Building, one of the campus's first two permanent buildings.

landmarks.name: Administration
facts: It opened in October 1960 as the Arts and Education Building, one of the campus's first two permanent buildings.

landmarks.name: Scurfield Hall
facts: It is home to the business school.
It opened on January 1, 1986, funded by donations from a homebuilder and his company.

landmarks.name: Yamnuska Hall
facts: It is a residence with a Starbucks, a Domino's and a Subway.
It opened in 2011 for second-year students.

landmarks.name: Mathison Hall
facts: It was built after a $20 million gift from a Calgary entrepreneur, announced in 2018.

landmarks.name: Earth Sciences
facts: The staff Faculty Club was on its 7th floor when it opened in 1973.

landmarks.name: Taylor Institute for Teaching and Learning
facts: It was launched for the university's 50th anniversary, on the site of the former Nickle Arts Museum.

landmarks.name: Crowsnest Hall
facts: It opened in 2015 as a residence for professional and graduate students.

landmarks.name: Olympus Hall
facts: It was built before the 1988 Winter Olympics as part of the athletes' Olympic Village.

landmarks.name: Mechanical Engineering Building
facts: It houses the mechanical and manufacturing engineering department of the Schulich School of Engineering.

landmarks.name: Aurora Hall
facts: It opened in 2015 for upper-year students, replacing the demolished Norquay, Brewster and Castle Halls.

landmarks.name: Rundle Hall
facts: It was built in the early 1960s when the university moved to its present campus.

landmarks.name: Kananaskis Hall
facts: It is one of the two oldest residences, built in the early 1960s when the university moved to its present campus.
